The actual is not something spatial as it is considered in mathematics; with such unreality as the things of mathematics are, neither concrete sensuous intuition nor philosophy occupies itself.

In such an unreal element there is then also only unreal truth, i.e. fixed, dead propositions; with each of them one can stop; the next begins anew for itself, without the first having moved itself onward to the other, and without a necessary connection arising in this way through the nature of the matter itself.
— Also, by virtue of that principle and element — and herein consists the formal aspect of mathematical evidence — knowing proceeds along the line of equality.

For the dead, because it does not move itself, does not arrive at differences of essence, not at essential opposition or inequality, hence not at the transition of the opposed into the opposed, not at qualitative, immanent, not at self-movement.
For it is magnitude, the inessential difference, which mathematics alone considers.

That it is the concept which divides space into its dimensions and determines the connections of them and in them — from this mathematics abstracts; it does not, e.g., consider the relation of the line to the surface; and where it compares the diameter of the circle with the circumference, it comes upon the incommensurability of the same, i.e. a relation of the concept, an infinite that escapes its determination.
zh: 这种有缺陷的认识的自明性，数学为它感到骄傲，也拿它向哲学吹嘘，这种自明性仅仅建立在它的目的贫乏和它的材料有缺陷之上，因此是哲学必须鄙弃的那一种。
——它的目的或概念是大小。
这恰恰是非本质的、无概念的关系。
知识的运动因此只在表面上进行，不触及事情本身，不触及本质或概念，因此不是以概念把握。
——数学用来给出那令人愉快的真理宝藏的材料，就是空间和一。
空间是那种定在，概念把自己的各种差别写进它里面，就像写进一个空洞的、死的要素，这些差别在其中同样是不动的、无生命的。
现实的东西并不是数学所考察的那种空间性的东西；无论是具体的感性直观还是哲学，都不去跟数学的物那样的非现实性打交道。
在这样一种非现实的要素里，也就只有非现实的真的东西，即固定下来的、死的命题；在每一个这样的命题那里都可以停下来；下一个命题则自为地重新开始，而第一个并没有自己向另一个继续运动，也没有以这种方式从事情本身的本性中产生出一种必然的联系。
——同样，由于那个原理和要素的缘故——数学的自明性中形式的东西正在于此——知识沿着相等的线前进。
因为死的东西并不自己运动，所以达不到本质的差别，达不到本质的对立或不等，因而达不到对立者向对立者的过渡，达不到质的、内在的运动，也达不到自我运动。
因为它就是大小，就是数学只考察的那种非本质的差别。
概念把空间分裂为它的各个维度，并规定这些维度之间的联系以及这些维度之中的联系，数学却从这一点抽象掉；例如它不考虑线与面的关系；而当它把圆的直径与圆周作比较时，就碰到两者的不可通约性，也就是概念的一种关系，一种逃避它的规定的无限者。

en: Immanent, so-called pure mathematics also does not set time as time over against space, as the second material of its consideration.

Applied mathematics does indeed treat of it, as of motion, and otherwise of other actual things; but it takes up the synthetic propositions, i.e. propositions of their relations, which are determined by their concept, from experience, and applies its formulas only to these presuppositions.

That the so-called proofs of such propositions, such as that of the equilibrium of the lever, of the relation of space and time in the motion of falling, etc., which it frequently gives, are given out and accepted as proofs, is itself only a proof of how great the need of proving is for cognition, because where it has nothing more, it also respects the empty semblance of it and thereby gains a satisfaction.

A critique of those proofs would be as remarkable as it is instructive, in order partly to cleanse mathematics of this false ornament, partly to show its limit and thereby the necessity of another knowing.
— As for time, of which one should think that, as the counterpart to space, it would constitute the material of the other part of pure mathematics, it is the existent concept itself.
The principle of magnitude, of concept-less difference, and the principle of equality, of abstract lifeless unity, is unable to concern itself with that pure unrest of life and absolute distinction.

This negativity therefore becomes, only as paralyzed, namely as the one, the second material of this cognition, which, an external doing, degrades the self-moving into material, in order now to have in it an indifferent, external, lifeless content.
zh: 内在的、所谓的纯粹数学，也没有把时间作为时间与空间对立起来，把它当作自己考察的第二种材料。
应用数学倒确实谈论时间，也谈论运动，以及在别处谈论其他现实的东西；但它从经验中接受那些综合的命题，即关于它们的关系的、由它们的概念所规定的命题，并且只把它的公式用到这些前提上。
这类命题——例如杠杆的平衡、下落运动中空间与时间的关系等等——的所谓证明，应用数学常常给出，却被当作证明提出并接受下来，这件事本身只是一个证明，说明认识对证明的需要有多大，因为认识在没有更多东西的时候，也会看重证明的空洞假象，并由此得到一种满足。
对这些证明的批判，会既值得注意，也同样有教益，一方面可以把数学从这种虚假的装饰中清洗干净，另一方面可以指出它的界限，并由此得出另一种知识的必然性。
——至于时间，人们会以为，它作为与空间相对的对应物，会构成纯粹数学另一部分的材料，而它其实就是定在着的概念本身。
大小、即无概念的区别这一原理，以及相等、即抽象的无生命的统一这一原理，都无法去跟生命的那种纯粹不安和绝对区分打交道。
因此这种否定性只是作为被麻痹了的、也就是作为一的东西，才成为这种认识的第二种材料，而这种认识作为一种外在的行为，把自身运动着的东西贬低为材料，为的是现在在它上面拥有一种无关紧要的、外在的、无生命的内容。

en: Philosophy, by contrast, does not consider the inessential determination, but it.
Insofar as it is essential; its element and content is not the abstract or the unreal, but the actual, self-positing and inwardly living, determinate being in its concept.
It is the process that produces for itself its moments and runs through them, and this whole movement constitutes the positive and its truth.
This therefore includes in itself just as much the negative, that which would be called the false if it could be considered as something from which one is to abstract.

The vanishing is rather itself to be considered as essential, not in the determination of something fixed that is to be left lying cut off from the true, outside it, one knows not where, just as the true is also not [to be considered] as the dead positive resting on the other side.
Appearance is the coming-to-be and passing-away that itself does not come to be and pass away, but is in itself and constitutes the actuality and movement of the life of truth.
The true is thus the bacchanalian whirl in which no member is not drunk; and because each, in separating itself, equally immediately dissolves itself, it is equally the transparent and simple repose.

In the judgment of that movement the individual shapes of spirit as well as the determinate thoughts indeed do not persist, but they are just as much positive necessary moments as they are negative and vanishing.

— In the whole of the movement, taken as repose, that which distinguishes itself in it and gives itself particular determinate being is preserved as something that recollects itself, whose determinate being is the knowledge of itself, just as this is equally immediately determinate being.
zh: 与此相反，哲学考察的不是非本质的规定，而是它。
只要它是本质的；它的要素和内容不是抽象的东西或非现实的东西，而是现实的东西、自己设定自己并在自身中活着的东西，是处在自己的概念中的定在。
它就是那个过程，它为自己产生出自己的各个环节，并把这些环节经历一遍，而整个这一运动构成了肯定的东西及其真理。
所以真理同样把否定的东西，也就是把那种会被称为虚假的东西，包含在自身之中，如果它可以被看作一种应当从它抽象掉的东西的话。
消失着的东西倒不如说本身就应该被看作本质的，而不是要在一种固定之物的规定中去考察，这种固定之物应当被从真的东西上割断，留在它之外，谁也不知道在什么地方，正如真的东西也不是那在另一边静止着的、死的肯定的东西。
现象就是产生和消逝，它本身并不产生也不消逝，而是自在的，并且构成真理的生命的现实性和运动。
真的东西因此就是酒神的狂乱，其中没有一个成员不是醉的；而因为每一个成员在把自己分离出来时，也同样直接地消解自己，所以它同样是透明的、单纯的宁静。
在那运动的审判中，精神的各个个别形态以及那些被规定的思想固然并不持存，但它们同样也是积极的、必然的环节，正如它们是消极的、消失着的。
——在运动的整体中，如果把它理解为宁静，那么在其中区分自己并给自己以特殊定在的东西，就是作为回忆着自身的东西被保存下来的，它的定在就是关于自身的知识，正如这种知识同样直接地就是定在。

en: Of the method of this movement, or of science, it might seem necessary to state the several [points] in advance.
But its concept already lies in what has been said, and its proper exposition belongs to the Logic, or is rather this itself.
For the method is nothing other than the construction of the whole, set up in its pure essentiality.
But of what has so far been current on this matter, we must be conscious that even the system of representations relating to what philosophical method is belongs to a vanished formation.

— If this should sound at all boastful or revolutionary, a tone I know myself to be far from, it is to be considered that the scientific pomp which mathematics lent — of definitions, divisions, axioms, series of theorems, their proofs, principles, and the inferring and concluding from them — is at least outdated even in opinion itself.
Even if its unfitness is not clearly seen, no use or little use is made of it any more, and if it is not disapproved in itself, it is still not loved.
And we must have the prejudice in favour of the excellent, that it puts itself into use and makes itself liked.
But it is not hard to see that the manner of setting up a proposition, adducing grounds for it, and refuting the opposite one equally by grounds, is not the form in which truth can appear.
Truth is the movement of itself upon itself; but that method is cognition that is external to the material.

Therefore it is proper to mathematics, which, as remarked, has the concept-less relation of magnitude to its principle and dead space as well as the equally dead one as its material, and it must be left to it.

It may also remain, in a freer manner, i.e. more mixed with arbitrariness and contingency, in common life, in a conversation or historical instruction, more [serving] curiosity than cognition, as roughly a preface also is.

In common life consciousness has cognitions, experiences, sensuous concretions, also thoughts, principles, in general such things as its content, which count as something present-at-hand or as a firm, resting being or essence, it runs on partly along these, partly interrupts the connection through free arbitrariness over such content and behaves as an external determining and handling of it.
It traces it back to something certain, even if only the sensation of the moment, and conviction is satisfied when it has arrived at a resting point known to it.
zh: 关于这一运动的方法、或者说关于科学的方法，也许看来有必要事先把其中较多的内容说出来。
但它的概念已经包含在说过的东西里，而它本来的阐述属于逻辑学，或者不如说就是逻辑学本身。
因为方法不是别的，就是整体的构造，是在它纯粹的本质性中建立起来的。
但对于在这个问题上迄今通行的那套东西，我们必须意识到：就连那些与何为哲学方法相关的表象的体系，也属于一种已经湮没无闻的教养。
——如果这话听来有点自夸或革命的味道——我自知与这种腔调相去甚远——，那就得想一想：数学所提供的那种科学排场——定义、划分、公理、定理的系列、它们的证明、原理，以及从这些原理出发的推论和推理——，至少在意见本身里也已经过时了。
即使它的不适用还没有被清楚地看出，人们毕竟不再运用它、或者很少运用它了，而即使它自在地没有遭到非议，它也毕竟不被人喜爱。
而我们必须抱有那种偏爱优异之物的成见：它会自行进入运用，并让自己受人喜爱。
但不难看出，那种提出一个命题、为它举出理由、并同样用理由去驳倒相反命题的做法，并不是真理能够出现在其中的形式。
真理是它自身在它自己身上的运动；而那种方法则是外在于材料的认识。
因此它是数学所固有的，数学正如已经指出的那样，把大小对其原则的那种无概念的关系，以及死空间和同样死的“一”，都当作自己的材料，所以它必须留给数学。
它也可以以更自由的做法、也就是更多地混入任意和偶然，留在日常生活里、在一次谈话或历史性的教导里，更多地属于好奇心而不是认识——一篇序言大约也是这样。
在日常生活里，意识以知识、经验、感性的具体物，还有思想、原理，总之以那种被看作现成的东西、或者被看作坚固的、静止的存在或本质的东西，为自己的内容，它一部分沿着这些内容继续下去，一部分则通过对这种内容的自由任意而打断联系，并且表现为对这种内容的一种外在的规定和处置。
它把内容归结到某种确定的东西上，哪怕那只是当下的感觉，而确信一旦到达一个它所熟悉的静止点，就得到了满足。

en: But if the necessity of the concept banishes the looser course of reasoning conversation as well as the stiffer course of scientific pomp, then it has already been recalled above that its place is not to be replaced by the non-method of divination and enthusiasm and the arbitrariness of prophetic speech, which despises not only that scientificity but scientificity in general.
zh: 但如果概念的必然性既驱逐了推理式谈话那种较松散的进程，也驱逐了科学铺张那种较僵硬的进程，那么前面已经提醒过：它的位置不应当由预感和狂热的非方法、以及预言式言论的任意来取代，而这种预言式言论蔑视的不仅是那种科学性，而是一般而言的科学性。

en: Just as little is — after the Kantian triplicity, first rediscovered by instinct, still dead, still not comprehended, has been raised to its absolute significance, and thereby the true form has at the same time been set up in its true content and the concept of science has emerged — any use of this form to be held as something scientific, a use through which we see it brought down to a lifeless schema, to a proper phantom, and the scientific organization to a table.

— This formalism, of which we have already spoken above in general and whose manner we want to specify more closely here, believes it has comprehended and expressed the nature and the life of a shape when it has predicated of it a determination of the schema as a predicate — be it subjectivity or objectivity, or also magnetism, electricity, etc., contraction or expansion, East or West and the like, which can be multiplied into infinity, because in this way every determination or shape can again be used with another as form or moment of the schema, and each can gratefully render the same service to the other — a circle of reciprocity, through which one learns neither what the matter itself is, nor what the one or the other is.

In this, on the one hand, sensuous determinations from ordinary intuition are taken up, which of course are supposed to mean something other than they say, on the other hand what is significant in itself, the pure determinations of thought, such as subject, object, substance, cause, the universal, etc., is used just as unexamined and uncritically as in common life, and like strengths and weaknesses, expansion and contraction, so that that metaphysics is just as unscientific as these sensuous representations.
zh: 同样，在康德那种最初由本能重新发现、但仍然是死的、仍然未被以概念把握的三重性被提升到它的绝对含义，从而真正的形式同时在其真正的内容中被建立起来、科学的概念也因此产生出来之后，对形式的这样一种运用也不能被看作某种科学的东西，通过这种运用，我们看到它被降格为无生命的图式、被降格为一个道地的幻影，而科学的组织则被降格为表格。

——这种形式主义，上面已经一般地说到过它、这里我们想更切近地指出它的做法，它以为只要它关于一个形态把图式的一种规定作为谓词说出来，就已经以概念把握并说出了这个形态的本性和生命，——不管那是主体性或客体性，或者还有磁力、电等等，是收缩或膨胀，是东方或西方之类，这些东西可以无限地增殖下去，因为按这种做法，每一种规定或形态都能在另一个那里重新充当图式的形式或环节，而每一个都感激地能为另一个提供同样的服务，——这是一个相互性的循环，通过它，人们既不知道事情本身是什么，也不知道这一个或那一个是什么。
在这里面，一部分是从普通直观中取来的感性规定，这些规定当然应当意味着与它们所说的不同的东西，另一部分则是那自在地有意义的东西，即思想的纯粹规定，如主体、客体、实体、原因、一般的东西等等，它们被不加审视地、不加批判地使用，就像在日常生活中一样，也像强弱、膨胀与收缩一样，以至于那种形而上学和这些感性的表象一样不科学。

en: Instead of the inner life and the self-movement of its determinate being, such a simple determinacy is now pronounced by intuition, i.e. here by sensuous knowledge, according to a superficial analogy, and this external and empty application of the formula is called construction.
— With such formalism the case is the same as with every [other].

How dull would the head have to be to which the theory that there are asthenic, sthenic and indirectly asthenic diseases and just as many healing plans could not be taught in a quarter of an hour, and which could not, since such instruction only recently sufficed for that, be transformed from a routinist into a theoretical doctor in this short time?

If the philosophy-of-nature formalism teaches, say, that the understanding is electricity, or that the animal is nitrogen, or also is equal to South or North etc., or represents it — whether as nakedly as it is expressed here, or also brewed together with more terminology —, then over such a power, which grasps together what seems far apart, and over the violence which resting sensuousness suffers through this combination and which thereby grants it the semblance of a concept, while the main thing, namely to express the concept itself or the meaning of the sensuous representation, is spared, over all this inexperience may fall into an admiring astonishment, revere in it a deep genius, and delight in the cheerfulness of such determinations, since they replace the abstract concept with something intuitive and make it more delightful, and congratulate itself on the surmised affinity of souls with such splendid doings.
The trick of such wisdom is learned as quickly as it is easy to practise it; once it is known, its repetition becomes as unbearable as the repetition of a magic trick one has seen through.

The instrument of this monotonous formalism is no harder to handle than a painter's palette on which there would be only two colours, say red and green, in order to colour a surface with the one if a historical piece were required, with the other if a landscape.

— It would be hard to decide what is greater here, the complacency with which everything in heaven, on earth and under the earth is daubed with such colour-brew, or the conceit about the excellence of this universal remedy; the one supports the other.

What this method brings forth — pasting the few determinations of the general schema onto everything heavenly and earthly, onto all natural and spiritual shapes, and in this way arranging everything into a series — is nothing less than a sun-clear report on the organism of the universe, namely a table that resembles a skeleton with little labels glued on, or the rows of closed boxes with their labels pinned on in a spice-merchant's shop, a table that is as clear as the one and the other and that, just as there flesh and blood are taken from the bones but here the equally non-living thing is hidden in the boxes, has also omitted or hidden the living essence of the matter.

— That this manner at the same time completes itself into monochrome absolute painting, in that it also, ashamed of the differences of the schema, sinks them as belonging to reflection into the emptiness of the absolute, so that pure identity, the formless white, may be produced, has already been remarked above.

That sameness of colour of the schema and its lifeless determinations, and this absolute identity, and the passing over from one to the other, is one as dead an understanding as the other and equally external cognition.
zh: 现在，代替它的定在的内在生命和自我运动，直观——这里也就是感性的知识——按照一种肤浅的类比说出这样一种单纯的规定性，而这种对公式的外在的、空洞的运用则被称为建构。
——这种形式主义的情形，和随便什么东西的情形是一样的。
头脑得多么迟钝，才会在一刻钟之内还学不会那种理论——即存在虚弱型、强壮型和间接虚弱型的疾病，以及同样多的治疗方案——，才会由于这样一种教导（不久之前它还足以做到这一点）而不能在这短短的时间里从一个墨守成规的医生变成一个理论医生呢？

如果自然哲学的形式主义教导说，知性就是电，或者动物就是氮，或者也等于南或北等等，或者说它表现着知性——不管是以这里所说的这种赤裸裸的方式，还是拌上更多的术语——，那么面对这样一种把显得相隔很远的东西抓到一起的力，面对静止的感性之物通过这种结合所遭受的、并因此赋予它一个概念的假象的那种暴力，而主要的事情，即说出概念本身或感性表象的含义，却被省掉了，面对这一切，没有经验的人也许会陷入惊叹的惊奇，在其中崇敬一种深刻的天才，并且为这类规定的欢快而感到快意，因为它们用直观的东西替换抽象的概念、让它变得更令人愉快，同时庆幸自己与这样一种了不起的做法有着预感到的灵魂亲缘。
这种智慧的窍门学起来很快，就像它做起来很容易一样；一旦它为人所知，它的重复就变得和重复一种已经被看穿的戏法一样令人难以忍受。
这种单调的形式主义的工具，并不比一个画家的调色板更难操作，那调色板上只会有两种颜色，比如红和绿，要一幅历史画就用前者去涂染一个平面，要一幅风景画就用后者。
——很难断定在这里哪一样更大：是把天上、地上和地下的一切都用这种颜料汤涂抹一遍的那种惬意，还是对这种万应灵药的优异的自负；前者扶持着后者。

这种方法——把一般图式的那几条规定粘贴到一切天上的和地上的东西、一切自然的和精神的形态上，并以此把一切都排入序列——所产生出来的东西，不是别的，正是一份关于宇宙有机体的明如白昼的报告，也就是一张表格，它像一具粘着小纸条的骷髅，或者像香料铺子里那一排排钉着标签的密封盒子，它和这二者一样清楚，而且就像在那里肉和血从骨头上被拿掉了、在这里那同样不是活的东西则被藏在盒子里一样，它也把事情的活生生的本质省略掉或藏起来了。
——这种做法同时也把自己完成成了单色的绝对绘画，因为它也羞于图式的那些差别，把它们作为属于反思的东西沉没到绝对者的空虚之中，以便把纯粹同一性、那无形式的白色建立起来——这一点上面已经提到过了。
图式及其无生命规定的这种同色，以及这种绝对同一性，还有从一个向另一个的过渡，都同样是死的知性，都同样是外在的认识。

en: But the excellent not only cannot escape the fate of being thus deprived of life and spirit and, so flayed, of seeing its skin taken up by lifeless knowledge and its vanity.

Rather, even in this very fate there is still to be recognized the violence which it exercises on minds, if not on spirits, as well as the formation into the universality and determinacy of form, in which its completion consists and which alone makes it possible that this universality is put to superficial use.
zh: 但优异的东西不仅逃不掉这样一种命运：被这样夺去生命、抽去精神，并且被这样剥了皮之后，还得看见自己的皮被无生命的知识及其虚荣拿去披上。
不如说，正是在这种命运本身之中，仍然可以认出它对人心、如果不是对诸精神所施加的强力，以及向形式的普遍性和规定性的形成，而它的完成就在于这种形式，并且唯有这种形式才使这种普遍性有可能被用于肤浅之事。

en: Science may organize itself only through the concept's own life; in it, the determinacy that is externally glued onto determinate being out of the schema is the self-moving soul of the fulfilled content.

The movement of what is consists, on the one hand, in becoming an other and thereby its own immanent content; on the other hand, it takes this unfolding, or this its determinate being, back into itself, i.e. makes itself into a moment and simplifies itself into determinacy.
In that movement, negativity is the distinguishing and the positing of determinate being; in this returning into itself, it is the becoming of determinate simplicity.

It is in this way that the content does not show its determinacy as received from an other and pinned on, but gives it to itself and ranks itself, out of itself, into a moment and into a place of the whole.

The tabular understanding keeps for itself the necessity and the concept of the content, that which constitutes the concrete, the actuality and living movement of the matter, which it ranks — or rather, it does not keep this for itself, but does not know it; for if it had this insight, it would surely show it.

It does not even know the need of that insight; otherwise it would leave off its schematizing, or at least would no longer know itself to be occupied with anything more than with an indication of content; it gives only the indication of content, but the content itself it does not supply.

— If the determinacy, even one such as magnetism, is something in itself concrete or actual, it has nevertheless sunk to something dead, since it is only predicated of another determinate being and is not cognized as the immanent life of this determinate being, or as it has in this being its own native and peculiar self-production and presentation.
To add this main thing, the formal understanding leaves to others.
— Instead of entering into the immanent content of the matter, it always surveys the whole and stands above the single determinate being of which it speaks, i.e. it does not see it at all.
But scientific cognition requires rather that one surrender oneself to the life of the object or, what is the same, that one have its inner necessity before oneself and express it.
Sinking thus into its object, it forgets that survey which is only the reflection of knowing out of the content into itself.

But sunk into the material and going on in its movement, it comes back into itself, but not earlier than in this, that the fulfilment or the content takes itself back into itself, simplifies itself into determinacy, lowers itself to one side of a determinate being, and passes over into its higher truth.
Thereby the simple whole that surveys itself emerges itself out of the wealth in which its reflection seemed lost.
zh: 科学只可以凭概念自身的生命来组织自己；在科学里，那种从图式出发被外在粘贴到定在上的规定性，就是充实了的内容的自己运动着的灵魂。
存在者的运动，一方面是要变成一个他者、并这样成为它内在的内容；另一方面是，它把这种展开、或者说把它这个定在收回到自身之中，也就是说，把自己造成一个环节，并把自己简化成规定性。
在那种运动里，否定性就是定在的区别与设定；在这种回到自身之中，它就是特定的单纯性的生成。
正是以这种方式，内容才不是把它的规定性表现为从另一个东西那里接受来、被别在它上面的，而是自己把规定性给自己，并凭自身把自己排成一个环节，排到整体的一个位置上。
表格式的知性把内容的必然性和概念留给自己，也就是说，把构成具体的东西、构成事情的现实性和活生生运动的那个东西留给自己，而那个东西正是它加以排列的；或者更确切地说，它并没有把它留给自己，而是根本不认识它；因为如果它有这种洞见，它想必会把它显示出来。
它甚至不知道有这种需要；否则它就会放弃自己的图式化做法，或者至少不再以为自己做的多过一份内容提要；它只给出内容提要，内容本身却不提供。
——如果规定性，哪怕像磁力这样的规定性，是自在具体或现实的规定性，那么它毕竟还是下降为某种死的东西了，因为它只是被用来述说另一个定在，而没有被认识为这个定在的内在生命，或者说，没有被认识为它在这个定在中拥有的那种它自己固有的、特有的自我产生和自我展示。
而把这件主要的事情添加上去，形式的知性则留给别人去做。
——它不深入事情的内在内容，反而总是对整体一览无余，并且站在它所谈论的个别定在之上，也就是说，它根本看不见它。
但科学性的认识反而要求：把自己交给对象的生命，或者——这是一回事——把对象的内部必然性摆在面前并把它说出来。
它这样深入自己的对象，就忘掉了那种一览，而那种一览不过是知识从内容中回到自身里的反思。
但它沉入材料之中、在材料的运动里继续前行，就回到自身之中，不过并不是更早，而是在这一点上回到自身：充实或内容把自己收回到自身里，简化成规定性，把自己降为定在的一个方面，并过渡到它更高的真理之中。
这样一来，那个单纯的、对自己一览无余的整体，就自己从那种丰富中浮现出来，而它的反思在那丰富中似乎曾经迷失。

en: Through this in general, that, as was expressed above, substance is in itself subject, all content is its own reflection into itself.
The subsistence or the substance of a determinate being is self-equality; for its inequality with itself would be its dissolution.
But self-equality is pure abstraction; and this is thinking.

If I say quality, I say simple determinacy; through quality a determinate being is distinguished from another, or is a determinate being; it is for itself, or it subsists through this simplicity with itself.
But thereby it is essentially thought.
— In this it is comprehended that being is thinking; and into this falls the insight which ordinary concept-less talk of the identity of thinking and being is wont to lack.

— Now through the fact that the subsistence of determinate being is self-equality or pure abstraction, it is the abstraction of itself from itself, or it is itself its inequality with itself and its dissolution — its own inwardness and withdrawal into itself — its becoming.

— Through this nature of what is, and insofar as what is has this nature for knowing, this knowing is not the activity that handles the content as something foreign, not the reflection-into-itself out of the content; science is not that idealism which stepped into the place of the assertoric dogmatism as an assuring dogmatism, or the dogmatism of the certainty of itself; but in that knowing sees the content go back into its own inwardness, its activity is rather both sunk into the content, for it is the immanent self of the content, and at the same time returned into itself, for it is the pure self-equality in otherness; thus it is the cunning which, seeming to abstain from activity, looks on at how determinacy and its concrete life, precisely in that it supposes itself to be pursuing its self-preservation and its particular interest, is the perverted doing that dissolves itself and makes itself into a moment of the whole.
zh: 一般地说，正因为——像上面已经表述过的那样——实体在它自身那里就是主体，所以一切内容都是它自己的自身反思。
一个定在的持存或实体，就是自身等同；因为它与自身的不等同就会是它的解体。
但自身等同就是那纯粹的抽象；而这纯粹的抽象就是思维。
如果我说质，我说的就是单纯的规定性；凭借质，一个定在与另一个定在区别开来，或者说就是一个定在；它是自为的，或者说它凭这种单纯性而与自身持存。
但这样一来，它本质上就是思想。
——这里面就含有这一点：存在就是思维；而普通无概念地谈论思维与存在的同一性时通常所缺少的，正是这种洞见。
——现在，正因为定在的持存是自身等同或纯粹抽象，所以它就是它自己从自身中的抽象，或者说它本身就是它与自身的不等同和它的解体，——它自己的内在性和向自身中的收回，——它的生成。

——凭借存在者的这种本性，并且在存在者对知识具有这种本性的限度内，知识就不是那样一种把内容当作异己的东西来摆弄的活动，也不是那种从内容中抽身回到自身的反思；科学并不是那种观念论，即取代断言式的独断论而作为一种保证式的独断论、或者说作为自身确定性的独断论出现的那种观念论；不如说，由于知识看见内容回到它自己的内在性之中，知识的活动就既是沉入内容之中——因为它是内容的内在自身——，又是同时回到自身之中——因为它是他在中的纯粹自身等同；这样一来，它就是那种狡计：它仿佛不参与活动，却在一旁观看规定性及其具体的生命如何恰恰因为自以为是在追求自己的自我保持和特殊利益，而成了那种颠倒的做法，成了自我解体、把自己变成整体环节的做法。

en: If above the significance of the understanding was given on the side of the self-consciousness of substance, then from what has been said here its significance emerges on the side of the determination of substance as something that is.
— Determinate being is quality, self-equal determinacy or determinate simplicity, determinate thought; this is the understanding of determinate being.
Thereby it is nous, as which Anaxagoras first cognized the essence.

Those after him comprehended the nature of determinate being more determinately as eidos or idea, i.e. as determinate universality, species. The expression “species” seems to be somewhat too common and too little for the ideas, for the beautiful and the holy and the eternal, which were rampant at that time.

But in fact the idea expresses no more and no less than species. But we now often see an expression that definitely designates a concept despised and another preferred, which, even if it is only because it belongs to a foreign language, wraps the concept in fog and thereby sounds more edifying.
— Precisely in that determinate being is determined as species, it is simple thought; nous, simplicity, is substance.
By virtue of its simplicity or self-equality it appears as firm and abiding, but this self-equality is equally negativity; thereby that firm determinate being passes over into its dissolution.

Determinacy seems at first to be so only through relating itself to an other, and its movement seems to be done to it by a foreign violence; but that it has its otherness itself on it and is self-movement, this is precisely contained in that simplicity of thought itself; for this is the self-moving and self-distinguishing thought and the proper inwardness, the pure concept.
So the understanding is a becoming, and as this becoming it is reason.
zh: 如果说上文是从实体的自我意识这一方面给出了知性的含义，那么从在这里所说的东西就可以看出，知性在把实体规定为存在者这一方面的含义。
——定在是质，是自身等同的规定性或者特定的单纯性，是特定的思想；这就是定在的知性。
这样一来，它就是nous，阿那克萨戈拉最早把本质认作的就是它。
在他之后的人更确定地把定在的本性以概念把握为eidos或idea（观念），也就是特定的普遍性、种；“种”这个说法对于当时正泛滥的那些观念、对于美的东西、神圣的东西和永恒的东西来说，似乎太寻常、也太不够了。
但事实上，观念所表达的不比种更多也不更少；只不过这时我们常常看到，一个明确标示出某个概念的说法遭到鄙弃，另一个说法却受到偏爱——哪怕仅仅因为它属于一门外语——，而后者把概念裹进迷雾里，因而听起来更感化人。
——恰恰因为定在被规定为种，它就是单纯的思想；而nous、这种单纯性，就是实体。
由于它的单纯性或自身等同，它显得坚固而持久，但这种自身等同同样是否定性；由此，那种坚固的定在就过渡到它的解体之中。
规定性起初似乎只有通过它与一个他者发生关系才存在，而它的运动似乎是由一种外来的强力加在它身上的；但它自己身上就带着它的他在，并且是自我运动，这一点恰恰就包含在思想的这种单纯性本身之中；因为这种单纯性就是自己运动着、自己作出区别的思想，就是它自己的内在性，就是纯粹的概念。
所以，知性就是一种生成，而作为这种生成，它就是理性。

en: In this nature of what is — namely, to be its concept in its being — lies the fact that logical necessity holds at all; it alone is the rational and the rhythm of the organic whole, it is just as much knowledge of the content as the content is concept and essence — or it alone is the speculative.

— The concrete shape, moving itself, makes itself into simple determinacy; thereby it raises itself to logical form and is in its essentiality; its concrete determinate being is only this movement and is immediately logical determinate being.

It is therefore unnecessary to put formalism on the concrete content from outside; the former is in itself the passing over into the latter, which however ceases to be this external formalism, because the form is the native becoming of the concrete content itself.
zh: 就在存在者的这种本性里，即在自己的存在中就是自己的概念，逻辑必然性才一般地存在；唯有它才是理性的东西和有机整体的节奏，它既是内容的知识，内容也同样是概念和本质，——或者说，唯有它才是思辨的东西。
——具体的形态自己运动着，把自己造成单纯的规定性；它由此把自己提升为逻辑形式，并且处于自己的本质性之中；它的具体定在只是这一运动，并且直接就是逻辑的定在。
因此没有必要从外面给具体内容套上形式主义；前者自身就是向它的过渡，而它却不再是这样外在的形式主义，因为形式就是具体内容自身所固有的生成。

en: This nature of scientific method — partly to be inseparable from the content, partly to determine its rhythm through itself — has, as already noted, its proper presentation in speculative philosophy.
— What is said here does indeed express the concept, but can count as no more than an anticipated assurance.

Its truth does not lie in this partly narrative exposition, and is therefore just as little refuted when it is asserted to the contrary that this is not so but that matters stand thus and thus, when customary representations are brought to mind and recounted as settled and well-known truths, or else something new is dished up out of the shrine of inner divine intuition and asserted.

— Such a reception is usually the first reaction of a knowing to which something was unknown, against that thing, in order to save freedom and one's own insight, one's own authority against the foreign (for it is under this shape that what is now first taken up appears) — also in order to remove the semblance and the kind of shame that is supposed to lie in the fact that something has been learned; just as in the applauding acceptance of the unknown, the reaction of the same kind consists in what in another sphere was the ultra-revolutionary talking and acting.
zh: 科学方法的这种本性，即一方面与内容不可分离，另一方面又通过自身规定自己的节奏，正如已经提到过的，在思辨哲学中才有它本来的展示。
——这里所说的虽然表达了概念，却只能算是一种预先的保证。
它的真理并不在这种部分地属于叙述的阐发里，因此，如果有人相反地断言情况并非如此，而是如此那般，如果有人把习惯的表象当作已成定论的和已知的真理重新提起并复述，或者还从内心神圣直观的神龛里端出什么新东西来加以断言，它也同样没有被驳倒。
——这样一种接受，通常是知识对自己本来不熟悉的东西的最初反弹，为的是保住自由和自己的识见、自己的权威，去对抗外来的权威（因为现在最初被接受的东西就是以这种形态出现的），——也是为了消除那种假象和那种羞辱，仿佛学习什么东西是丢人的；正如在对未知东西报以掌声的接受那里，同类的反应就在于在另一个领域里曾是极端革命的言论和行动的那种东西。

en: What therefore matters in the study of science is to take the effort of the concept upon oneself.

It demands attention to it as such, to the simple determinations, e.g. of being-in-itself, of being-for-itself, of self-sameness, etc.; for these are pure self-movements that one could call souls, if their concept did not designate something higher than these.
To the habit of running on through representations, their interruption by the concept is just as troublesome as to formal thinking, which reasons back and forth in unreal thoughts.

That habit is to be called a material thinking, a contingent consciousness that is merely sunk in the material, so that it finds it hard to lift its own self cleanly out of the matter and to be with itself.

The other, reasoning, on the contrary, is freedom from the content and vanity about it; the effort is demanded of it to give up this freedom and, instead of being the arbitrarily moving principle of the content, to sink this freedom into the content, to let it move through its own nature, i.e. through the self as its own, and to contemplate this movement.

To renounce one's own intrusion into the immanent rhythm of the concepts, not to intervene in it through arbitrariness and otherwise acquired wisdom — this abstinence is itself an essential moment of attention to the concept.
zh: 因此，学习科学时的关键就在于，把概念的辛劳担到自己身上。
它要求关注概念本身，关注那些单纯的规定，例如自在存在、自为存在、自身等同等等；因为这些都是纯粹的自己运动，要不是它们的概念所指的东西比这些更高，人们本可以把它们叫作灵魂。
对于顺着表象一路跑下去的习惯来说，概念对它的打断，和对于在非现实的思想里来回推理的形式思维一样令人难受。
那种习惯可以叫作物质性的思维，一种偶然的意识，它只是沉没在材料里，因此对它来说很难同时从材料中把自己的自我干净地提出来，并留在自己那里。
另一面，即推理，则是对内容的自由和对内容的虚荣；它被要求付出努力，放弃这种自由，不再做任意推动内容的原则，而是把这种自由沉入内容之中，让内容通过自己的本性、即通过作为内容自己的自我而运动，并考察这一运动。
放弃自己插进概念的内在节奏里去，不通过任意和别处得来的智慧去干预它，这种克制本身就是关注概念的一个本质环节。

en: In the reasoning attitude, the two sides according to which conceptual thinking is opposed to it are to be made more noticeable.
— On the one hand, it behaves negatively toward the content it has taken up, and knows how to refute it and make it null.

That it is not so — this insight is the merely negative; it is the last, which does not itself go beyond itself to a new content; rather, in order to have a content again, something else must be taken up from somewhere.
It is the reflection into the empty I, the vanity of its knowing.
— But this vanity expresses not only that this content is vain, but also that this insight itself is vain; for it is the negative that does not see the positive in itself.

Because this reflection does not win its own negativity as content, it is not in the matter at all but always beyond it; it therefore imagines that, with the assertion of emptiness, it is always further along than a content-rich insight, whereas, as shown just now, in conceptual thinking the negative belongs to the content itself and, both as its immanent movement and determination and as the whole of these, is the positive.
Taken as result, it is what comes out of this movement, the determinate negative and thus equally a positive content.
zh: 在推理的态度上，有两个方面需要说得更明白，以概念把握的思维正是按照这两个方面与它相对立。
——一方面，它对所把握的内容取否定的态度，懂得驳倒它、使它化为乌有。
事情并非如此，这种识见只是否定性的东西；它是最后的东西，本身并不超出自己走向新的内容；相反，为了重新有一个内容，必须从某处拿来别的东西。
这是向空洞的我的反思，是它的知识的虚荣。
——但这种虚荣不仅表达出这个内容是虚的，也表达出这种识见本身是虚的；因为它是否定性的东西，并不在自己身上看到肯定性的东西。
由于这种反思并没有把自身的否定性变成内容，它根本就不在事情之中，而总是已经在事情之外；因此它自以为，凭着断言空洞，自己总比一种内容丰富的识见走得更远，反之，正如刚才指出的，在以概念把握的思维里，否定性的东西属于内容本身，并且既作为它内在的运动和规定、又作为这些规定的整体，是肯定性的东西。
作为结果来把握，它就是出自这一运动的东西，是特定的否定，因而同样是一个肯定性的内容。

en: But in view of the fact that such thinking has a content — be it of representations or of thoughts or of a mixture of both — it has another side that makes comprehension difficult for it.
The remarkable nature of this side is closely connected with the essence of the idea itself given above, or rather expresses it as it appears as the movement that thinking apprehension is.

— For just as in its negative behaviour, of which we were just speaking, reasoning thinking is itself the self into which the content returns, so on the contrary in its positive cognition the self is a represented subject to which the content relates as accident and predicate.
This subject constitutes the basis to which the content is tied and on which the movement runs back and forth.
It is otherwise in conceptual thinking.

Since the concept is the object's own self, which presents itself as its becoming, it is not a resting subject that motionlessly bears the accidents, but the concept that moves itself and takes its determinations back into itself.

In this movement that resting subject itself goes under; it enters into the differences and the content and instead constitutes the determinacy, i.e. the differentiated content as well as its movement, instead of standing still over against it.
The firm ground that reasoning has in the resting subject thus falters, and only this movement itself becomes the object.
The subject that fills out its content ceases to go beyond it, and cannot have yet other predicates or accidents.
The scatteredness of the content is conversely thereby bound under the self; it is not the universal that, free from the subject, would accrue to several.
The content is thus in fact no longer predicate of the subject, but is the substance, is the essence and the concept of that of which there is talk.

Representational thinking — since it is its nature to run on through the accidents or predicates and, with right, to go beyond them, because they are nothing more than predicates and accidents — is checked in its running on when what has the form of a predicate in the proposition is the substance itself.
It suffers, to put it that way, a counter-thrust.

Starting from the subject, as if this were to remain the underlying ground, it finds — since the predicate is rather the substance — the subject passed over into the predicate and thereby sublated; and since what seems to be a predicate has thus become the whole and independent mass, thinking cannot wander about freely but is held up by this weight.

— Otherwise, the subject is first laid down as the objective fixed self; from here the necessary movement proceeds to the manifoldness of the determinations or predicates; here the knowing I itself steps into the place of that subject and is the connecting of the predicates and the subject that holds them together.

But since that first subject enters into the determinations themselves and is their soul, the second subject, namely the knowing one, finds still present in the predicate that subject with which it wanted to be already done and beyond which it wanted to return into itself; and instead of being able to be the active one in the moving of the predicate — as reasoning whether this or that predicate should be attached to that one — it has rather still to do with the self of the content, and is not to be for itself but together with this.
zh: 但就这种思维有一个内容而言——不论是表象的内容还是思想的内容，或是两者的混合——，它还有另外一面，这一面使以概念把握对它来说变得困难。
这一面的奇特本性与上面所说的观念本身的本质紧密相关，或者说它毋宁表达了这一本质，即本质如何表现为思维着的把握所是的那一运动。
——因为正如在它那否定性的态度中（刚才谈的就是这个），推理的思维本身就是内容返回于其中的那个自我，同样，在它肯定性的认识中，自我则是一个被表象的主体，内容作为偶性和谓词与这个主体相关。
这个主体构成一个基础，内容被系在上头，运动也在这个基础上来回跑。
在以概念把握的思维里，情形就不同了。
既然概念是对象自己的自我，而这自我把自己展示为对象的生成，那么它就不是一个静止的主体，不动地承载着各种偶性，而是自己运动着、并把自己的各种规定收回自身之内的概念。
在这一运动中，那个静止的主体本身也消亡了；它进入各种差别和内容之中，反倒构成了规定性，即构成了有差别的内容以及这内容的运动，而不是站在它对面不动。
于是，推理在静止的主体那里拥有的稳固基地动摇了，只有这一运动本身成了对象。
充实了自己内容的主体，不再超出这个内容，也不能再有别的谓词或偶性。
内容的分散状态由此反过来被束缚在自我之下；它并不是那种脱离主体而可以属于许多东西的普遍者。
因此，内容实际上不再是主体的谓词，而是实体，是所谈之物的本质和概念。
表象的思维，由于它的本性就是顺着偶性或谓词一路跑下去，并且有理由超出它们，因为它们无非是谓词和偶性，——当命题中具有谓词形式的东西就是实体本身时，这种思维就在它的一路跑动中被拦住了。
用表象的方式来说，它遭到了一次反冲。
它从主体出发，仿佛这个主体始终留在底下作根据，可是由于谓词毋宁说就是实体，它就发现主体已经过渡为谓词，并因此被扬弃了；而这样一来，那看起来是谓词的东西已经成了完整而独立的一团，思维就不能自由地四处游荡，而是被这种重量拦住了。
——在别的情况下，主体首先被设定为对象性的固定自我；必然的运动从这里出发，走向各种规定或谓词的多样性；在这里，认识着的我就代替了那个主体，成了谓词的联结者和把它们持住的主体。
但是，由于那第一个主体进入了各种规定本身，并且是它们的灵魂，第二个主体、即认识着的主体，就在谓词中发现了那个它本来想已经了结、并想越过它返回自身的主体；而且，它不能在做谓词的运动中充当那个动手的人——像推理那样考虑该给那个主体加上这个还是那个谓词——，反而还须与内容自身的自我打交道，不该自为地存在，而该与这个自我在一起。

en: Formally, what has been said can be expressed thus: that the nature of judgment or of the proposition in general, which encloses within itself the difference of subject and predicate, is destroyed by the speculative proposition, and the identical proposition into which the former turns contains the counter-thrust against that relation.
— This conflict between the form of the proposition in general and the unity of the concept that destroys it is similar to the one that takes place in rhythm between metre and accent.
Rhythm results from the hovering middle and the unification of the two.

Thus in the philosophical proposition too the identity of subject and predicate should not destroy their difference, which the form of the proposition expresses, but their unity [should] emerge as a harmony.

The form of the proposition is the appearance of the determinate sense, or the accent that distinguishes its fulfilment; but that the predicate expresses the substance and the subject itself falls into the universal is the unity in which that accent dies away.
zh: 从形式上，说过的东西可以这样来表达：判断或一般命题的那种本性，它自身中包含着主体和谓词的差别，被思辨命题毁掉，而前者所变成的那种同一命题，则包含着对那种关系的反冲。
——一般命题的形式与那毁掉它的概念之统一之间的这种冲突，类似于节奏中在格律与重音之间发生的那种冲突。
节奏是从两者那种悬浮的中间和统一中产生出来的。
所以在哲学命题中，主体和谓词的同一性也不应当毁掉它们的差别，即命题的形式所表达的那种差别，而它们的统一则〔应当〕作为和谐而出现。
命题的形式是特定含义的现象，或者说，是区分出它的充实的那个重音；但谓词表达实体、主体本身落入普遍者，这就是那种统一，那个重音在其中渐渐消逝。

en: To illustrate what has been said by examples: in the proposition “God is being”, the predicate is “being”; it has substantial significance, in which the subject melts away.
Here “being” is not supposed to be a predicate but the essence; thereby God seems to cease to be what he is through the position of the proposition, namely the fixed subject.

— Thinking, instead of advancing in the transition from subject to predicate, feels itself, since the subject is lost, rather checked, and thrown back upon the thought of the subject because it misses it; or, since the predicate itself is uttered as a subject, as being, as essence, which exhausts the nature of the subject, it finds the subject immediately in the predicate as well; and now, instead of having gone into itself in the predicate and received the free position of ratiocination, it is all the more absorbed in the content, or at least the demand is present that it be absorbed in it.
— So too when it is said: the actual is the universal, the actual passes away as subject in its predicate.

The universal is not supposed merely to have the meaning of the predicate, so that the proposition would state that the actual is universal; rather the universal is supposed to express the essence of the actual.

— Thinking therefore loses its firm objective ground, which it had in the subject, the more it is thrown back upon it in the predicate and in the predicate returns not into itself but into the subject of the content.
zh: 为了用例子说明所说的东西：在“上帝是存在”这个命题里，谓词是“存在”；它具有实体性的含义，主体在其中消融了。
在这里，“存在”不应当是谓词，而应当是本质；这样一来，上帝似乎就不再是它通过命题中的位置而所是的东西，即那个固定的主体。
——思维本来要在从主体到谓词的过渡中往前走，现在因为主体失去了，反倒觉得自己受了阻碍，并且因为惦记着主体而被抛回到主体的思想上去；或者，由于谓词本身是作为主体、作为存在、作为本质而被说出来的，而这穷尽了主体的本性，思维就直接在谓词中也发现了主体；而现在，思维并不是在谓词中回到自身、从而获得推理的那种自由位置，反倒更深地沉浸到内容里，或者至少存在着这样的要求：要沉浸到它里面去。
——同样，当人们说“现实的东西是普遍者”时，现实的东西作为主体就在它的谓词中消逝了。
普遍者不应当只具有谓词的含义，仿佛这个命题说的是：现实的东西是普遍的；相反，普遍者应当表达现实的东西的本质。
——因此，思维越是在谓词中被抛回到它曾在主体那里拥有的那种牢固的对象性地基上，并且在谓词中不是回到自身、而是回到内容的主体中去，它也就越是失去这种基地。

en: On this unfamiliar checking rest for the most part the complaints about the unintelligibility of philosophical writings, provided that the other conditions of formation for understanding them are present in the individual.

In what has been said we see the ground of the quite determinate reproach often made against them, that several things must first be read repeatedly before they can be understood — a reproach that is supposed to contain something improper and final, so that, if it is well founded, it admits of no further rejoinder.
— It is clear from the above what the state of the matter is.
The philosophical proposition, because it is a proposition, awakens the opinion of the ordinary relation of subject and predicate and of the habitual comportment of knowing.

This comportment and the opinion belonging to it are destroyed by the proposition's philosophical content; the opinion discovers that it is meant differently from the way it meant it, and this correction of its opinion compels knowing to return to the proposition and now to grasp it differently.
zh: 对哲学著作不可理解的抱怨，大部分就基于这种不习惯的阻碍，只要个体身上具备着理解它们所需的其他教养条件。
我们在所说的话里看到了人们常常对它们提出的那个十分确定的指责的根据，即许多地方必须先反复读，然后才能被理解——这个指责据说含有某种不合体统、最终的东西，因此它只要有根据，就不容再有反驳。
——从上面所说的可以看出，这件事究竟是怎么回事。
哲学命题，因为它是命题，就唤起了关于主体和谓词的通常关系以及知识的习惯态度的那种意见。
这种态度和属于它的意见，被命题的哲学内容毁掉了；意见发觉，事情被意谓得和它所意谓的不一样，而这种对它的意见的纠正，迫使知识回到命题上来，并且现在用另一种方式把握这个命题。

en: A difficulty that ought to be avoided constitutes the mixing of the speculative and the ratiocinative manner, when what is said of the subject sometimes has the meaning of its concept, but at other times only the meaning of its predicate or accident.
— The one manner disturbs the other, and only that philosophical exposition would succeed in being plastic which strictly excluded the manner of the ordinary relation of the parts of a proposition.
zh: 一种本来应当避免的困难，构成了思辨方式和推理方式的混杂：关于主体所说的东西，时而具有它的概念的含义，时而又只具有它的谓词或偶性的含义。
——一种方式搅扰着另一种方式，而只有那种严格排除命题各部分的通常关系方式的哲学阐发，才会做到具有雕塑性。

en: In fact, non-speculative thinking too has its right, which is valid but is not heeded in the manner of the speculative proposition.
That the form of the proposition is sublated must not happen only in an immediate way, not through the mere content of the proposition.
Rather, this opposed movement must be expressed; it must not be merely that inward checking, but this return of the concept into itself must be exhibited.
This movement, which constitutes what the proof was otherwise supposed to accomplish, is the dialectical movement of the proposition itself.
It alone is the actual speculative [element], and only the utterance of it is speculative exposition.
As proposition, the speculative is only the inward checking and the not-existing return of the essence into itself.
We therefore often find ourselves referred by philosophical expositions to this inner intuition, and thereby spared the exposition of the dialectical movement of the proposition that we demanded.

— The proposition is supposed to express what the true is, but essentially it is subject; as this, it is only the dialectical movement, this self-generating, onward-leading and into-itself-returning course.
— In other cognition, the proof constitutes this side of expressed inwardness.
But after the dialectic has been separated from the proof, the concept of philosophical proving has in fact been lost.
zh: 事实上，非思辨的思维也有它的权利，这权利是有效的，只是在思辨命题的方式中未被顾及。
命题的形式被扬弃，这件事不应当只以直接的方式发生，不应当仅仅通过命题的内容而发生。
相反，这种对立着的运动必须被说出来；它不应当只是那种内在的阻碍，而概念的这种回到自身则必须被表述出来。
这种运动构成了通常本该由证明来完成的东西，它就是命题自身的辩证运动。
只有它才是现实的思辨的东西，而且只有把这种运动说出来，才是思辨的阐述。
作为命题，思辨的东西只是那种内在的阻碍，以及本质那种并不定在的回到自身。
因此我们常常看到，哲学阐发把我们打发到这种内在直观上去，从而省掉了我们要求的那种对命题的辩证运动的阐述。
——命题应当表达真的东西是什么，但真的东西本质上就是主体；作为主体，它只是辩证的运动，即这种自己产生自己、引导自己向前、并回到自身中去的进程。
——在别的认识那里，证明构成了这种被说出来的内在性的方面。
但是，在辩证法与证明被分开之后，哲学证明的概念事实上也就丢失了。

en: On this point it may be recalled that the dialectical movement likewise has propositions as its parts or elements; the difficulty pointed out therefore seems always to return and to be a difficulty of the matter itself.
— This is similar to what occurs in ordinary proof, that the grounds it uses themselves again require a grounding, and so on into infinity.
But this form of grounding and conditioning belongs to that kind of proof from which the dialectical movement is different, and thus to external cognition.
As for this movement itself, its element is the pure concept; thereby it has a content that is through and through subject in its own self.
Thus no such content occurs here as would behave as an underlying subject and to which its meaning would belong as a predicate; the proposition is immediately only an empty form.
— Apart from the sensuously intuited or represented self, it is chiefly the name as name that designates the pure subject, the empty, concept-less One.

For this reason it can, e.g., be useful to avoid the name God, because this word is not immediately at the same time a concept, but is the proper name, the fixed repose of the underlying subject; whereas, e.g., being or the One, singularity, the subject, etc., themselves also immediately intimate concepts.

— Even if speculative truths are stated of that subject, their content still lacks the immanent concept, because it is present only as a resting subject, and through this circumstance they easily take on the form of mere edification.

— From this side, then, the hindrance that lies in the habit of grasping the speculative predicate according to the form of the proposition, and not as concept and essence, can likewise be increased and diminished through the fault of philosophical exposition itself.
Exposition must, true to the insight into the nature of the speculative, retain the dialectical form and admit nothing except in so far as it is comprehended and is the concept.
zh: 这里可以提醒说，辩证运动同样以命题为自己的部分或要素；所以那个被指出来的困难看来总是在重新出现，并且是事情本身的一种困难。
——这和通常的证明里出现的情形相似：它所用的根据本身又需要有一种论证，如此一直下去，直到无限。
但提供根据和设置条件这种形式，属于那种辩证运动与之不同的证明，因而属于外在的认识。
至于辩证运动本身，它的要素是纯粹概念；这样一来它就有了一个内容，而这个内容彻头彻尾在自身那里就是主体。
所以这里不会出现这样一种内容：它充当被置于底下的主体，而它的含义则作为谓词归属于它；命题直接只是一个空洞的形式。
——除了感性直观到的自身或被表象的自身之外，主要是作为名称的名称在指称纯粹主体，即那个空洞的、无概念的“一”。
出于这个理由，比如说，避免使用上帝这个名字可能是有益的，因为这个词并不直接同时是概念，而是本来的名称，是被置于底下的主体那种固定的静止；反之，比如说存在或一、单一性、主体等等，本身也直接暗示着概念。
——即使关于那个主体说出了思辨的真理，这些真理的内容也仍然缺少内在的概念，因为内容只是作为静止的主体而存在，而它们由于这种情况很容易取得纯然说教的形式。
——所以从这一方面看，那种存在于习惯之中的障碍——即按照命题的形式、而不是作为概念和本质去把握思辨的谓词——也可能由于哲学讲论本身的过失而被增大和减小。
阐述必须忠于对思辨本性的洞见，保持辩证的形式，并且除了在它被以概念把握、并且就是概念的情况下，不纳入任何东西。

en: As much as reasoning behaviour, so too the non-reasoning conceit of settled truths hinders the study of philosophy — truths to which the possessor thinks he need not return, but which he lays down as a foundation and believes he can utter and by them judge and pronounce.
From this side it is especially necessary that philosophy be made into a serious business again.
Of all sciences, arts, skills and crafts the conviction holds that, in order to possess them, a manifold effort of learning and practising them is necessary.

In regard to philosophy, on the other hand, the prejudice now seems to prevail that, although everyone has eyes and fingers, and although he gets leather and tools, he is for that reason not able to make shoes, yet everyone immediately understands how to philosophize and to judge philosophy, because he possesses the standard for it in his natural reason — as if he did not likewise possess the standard of a shoe in his foot.
— It seems to be precisely in the lack of knowledge and of study that the possession of philosophy is placed, and that philosophy stops where the former begin.

It is often held to be a formal, content-less knowing, and there is a great lack of the insight that whatever is truth in content in any knowledge and science can deserve this name only if it has been produced by philosophy; that the other sciences, let them try reasoning without philosophy as much as they will, are unable without it to have life, spirit, truth in them.
zh: 与推理式的态度一样，对哲学的研究有害的，是那种不作推理的、对已成定论的真理的臆想：拥有这种真理的人以为没有必要再回头去谈它们，而是把它们当作根据，并且相信自己能够说出它们，还能凭它们来评判和裁断。
从这一方面看，特别有必要重新把哲学思考当成一件严肃的事情来做。
对于一切科学、艺术、技能和手艺，人们都抱着这样的确信：要拥有它们，就必须在学习它们和练习它们上做出多方面的努力。
与此相反，就哲学而言，现在似乎流行着这样一个偏见：尽管每个人都有眼睛和手指，而且即使他得到皮革和工具，他也还是不会做鞋，但每个人却直接懂得哲学思考，懂得评判哲学，因为他在自己的自然理性上就拥有做这件事的尺度——就好像他在自己的脚上同样并不拥有鞋的尺度似的。
——看来恰恰是把对哲学的拥有放进了知识和研究的缺乏之中，而且哲学恰好在知识和研究开始的地方就终止了。
它常常被看作一种形式性的、没有内容的知识，而人们非常缺乏这样一种洞见：无论在哪一种知识和科学里，凡在内容上是真理的东西，只有当它是由哲学产生出来的时候，才配得上真理这个名称；其他科学尽可以不要哲学而试着去推理，想试多少就试多少，但若没有哲学，它们就不能在自己内部拥有生命、精神和真理。

en: In regard to philosophy proper, we see the immediate revelation of the divine and sound common sense — which has exerted and cultivated itself neither with other knowing nor with philosophy proper — regard themselves, for the long path of formation, for the movement as rich as it is deep through which spirit arrives at knowing, directly as a perfect equivalent and as good a surrogate as chicory is praised for being a surrogate of coffee.

It is not pleasant to note that ignorance, and formless and tasteless crudeness itself, which is incapable of holding its thinking fast to an abstract proposition, still less to the connection of several, assures us now of the freedom and tolerance of thinking, and now of genius.

The latter, as now in philosophy, notoriously once raged in poetry as well; instead of poetry, however, if the producing of this genius had any sense, it brought forth trivial prose, or, if it went beyond that, mad speeches.

Thus now a natural philosophizing, which holds itself too good for the concept and through its lack takes itself for an intuitive and poetic thinking, brings to market arbitrary combinations of an imagination merely disorganized by thought — formations that are neither fish nor flesh, neither poetry nor philosophy.
zh: 就真正的哲学来说，我们看到，对于教养的漫长道路，对于精神借以达致知识的既丰富又深刻的运动，神圣之物的直接启示和健全的常识——后者既没有在别的知识上、也没有在真正的哲学思考上费过心并受过教养——都直接把自己看作十足的等价物和同样好的替代品，正如菊苣被称赞为咖啡的替代品一样。
令人不快的是看到，无知本身，以及那种既无形式又无趣味的粗野——它无力把自己的思想固定在一个抽象命题上，更无力固定在多个命题的关联上——时而又保证自己是思想的自由和宽容，时而又保证自己是天才。
后一种东西，正如现在在哲学里那样，众所周知当年在诗里也同样盛行；但如果这种天才的创作还有什么意义的话，它生产出来的并不是诗，而是平庸的散文，或者，如果它超出了散文，就是疯话。
现在，这样一种自然的哲学思考——它自视太高，不屑于概念，并且由于缺少概念而自认为是一种直观的、诗意的思维——拿到市场上来的是想象力的任意组合，而这种想象力只是被思想弄得失去了组织——这些产物既不是鱼也不是肉，既不是诗也不是哲学。

en: On the other hand, flowing on in the calmer bed of sound common sense, natural philosophizing serves up a rhetoric of trivial truths.

If the insignificance of these is held up to it, it assures us in return that the sense and the fulfilment are present in its heart, and must likewise be present in others, since it thinks it has said the last things with the innocence of the heart and the purity of conscience and the like, against which no objection takes place nor anything further can be demanded.
But the point was that the best should not remain within, but be brought to light out of this shaft.
To bring forward last truths of that kind — this effort could long ago have been spared, for they are long since to be found, say, in the catechism, in the proverbs of the people, etc.
— It is not difficult to grasp such truths in their indeterminacy or crookedness, often to point out to their consciousness the directly opposite one within itself.

In trying to draw itself out of the confusion that is set up in it, it falls into new confusion and will probably come out with the declaration that things are decidedly thus and so, but that those are sophistries — a catchword of common sense against cultivated reason, as the expression “dreams” is one that the ignorance of philosophy has noted down for it once and for all.

— In appealing to feeling, its inner oracle, it is finished with anyone who does not agree; it must declare that it has nothing further to say to one who does not find and feel the same in himself; — in other words, it tramples the root of humanity underfoot.
For the nature of this humanity is to insist on agreement with others, and its existence only in the achieved commonality of consciousnesses.
The inhuman, the animal consists in remaining stuck in feeling and being able to communicate only through it.
zh: 相反，自然的哲学思考在健全常识那条更平静的河床里继续流淌，端出来的是一套平庸真理的修辞术。
如果有人向它指出这些真理的微不足道，它就反过来保证说，意义和充实就在它心里，而且必定也这样在别人那里，因为它总以为凭着心的无辜、良心的纯净之类就已经说出了终极的东西，对此既不会有反驳，也不能再要求什么。
但要做的是让最好的东西不要留在内心里，而是从这座矿井里被开采到地面上来。
提出那一类终极真理，这番辛苦早就可以省掉了，因为它们早就可以在教义问答、民间谚语等等里面找到。
——要抓住这类真理的不确定或歪斜并不难，往往还能在它自己的意识里向它指出恰好相反的那一个。
它在努力把自己从被搅起的混乱里拉出来时，又会陷入新的混乱，而且很可能会爆出这样的话：事情确实就是如此这般，而那些则是诡辩——这是普通人的常识用来对付有教养的理性的一个口头禅，正如哲学的无知为哲学一劳永逸地记住了“做梦”这个说法一样。
——当它援引感觉这个它内心的神谕时，它对那个不赞同的人就已经了事了；它必须声明，对那个在自己身上找不到、也感觉不到同样东西的人，它没有什么可再说的；——也就是说，它把人性的根踩在脚下。
因为人性的本性就是要坚持与他人达成一致，而它的存在只在于已经达成的那种诸意识的共同性之中。
反人性的东西、动物性的东西就在于停留在感觉里，并且只能通过感觉来传达自己。

en: If a royal road to science were asked for, no more convenient one could be given than to rely on sound common sense and, in order incidentally also to keep pace with the times and with philosophy, to read reviews of philosophical writings, perhaps even their prefaces and first paragraphs; for the latter give the universal principles on which everything depends, while the former, besides the historical note, also give the assessment, which, just because it is an assessment, is beyond what is assessed.

This vulgar way makes itself comfortable in its dressing gown; but in high-priestly vestments the lofty feeling of the eternal, the holy, the infinite strides along — a way that is rather itself already the immediate being at the centre, the genius of deep original ideas and lofty flashes of thought.
Yet just as such depth does not as yet reveal the source of essence, so these rockets are not as yet the empyrean.
True thoughts and scientific insight are to be won only in the labour of the concept.

It alone can bring forth the universality of knowledge, which is neither the vulgar indeterminacy and wretchedness of common human understanding but formed and complete cognition, nor the uncommon universality of the disposition of reason that ruins itself through the laziness and self-conceit of genius, but the truth grown to its native form — which is capable of being the property of all self-conscious reason.
zh: 如果要问一条通往科学的御道，那么没有比这条更省事的了：信赖健全的人类知性，并且为了顺便也随时代和哲学一道前进，去读哲学著作的书评，甚至也许去读这些著作的序言和头几节；因为后者给出一切所依据的普遍原理，而前者除了历史性的说明之外还给出评判，这种评判甚至因为它是评判，就超出了被评判的东西。
这条平庸的道路穿着家常便服，自在得很；但永恒、神圣、无限的高昂情感却披着大祭司的法衣阔步前行——这是一条路，它毋宁说本身就已经是在中心里的直接存在，是深刻的原创观念和崇高思想闪光的天才气质。
不过，正如这样的深度还没有揭示出本质的源泉，这些火箭也还不是最高天。
真的思想和科学的识见只有在概念的劳动中才能获得。
唯有它才能产生出知识的普遍性，这种普遍性既不是普通人类知性那种平庸的不确定性和贫乏，而是有教养的、完整的认识，也不是那种因懒惰和天才的自负而败坏自身的理性禀赋的不普通的普遍性，而是长成到它本己形式的真理——它能够成为一切自我意识的理性的财产。

en: In placing that whereby science exists into the self-movement of the concept, the consideration that the cited and still other external aspects of our time's representations about the nature and shape of truth diverge from this, indeed are wholly contrary to it, seems to promise no favourable reception to an attempt to present the system of science in that determination.

Meanwhile I may consider that, if for instance the excellence of Plato's philosophy is sometimes placed in his scientifically worthless myths, there have also been times that are even called times of enthusiasm, in which the Aristotelian philosophy was esteemed for the sake of its speculative depth, and Plato's Parmenides, probably the greatest work of art of ancient dialectic, was held to be the true revelation and the positive expression of the divine life, and even amid much murkiness of what ecstasy produced, this misunderstood ecstasy was in fact supposed to be nothing other than the pure concept, — that furthermore the excellence of the philosophy of our time places its value itself in scientificity and, even if others take it otherwise, in fact makes itself valid only through it.
Thus I may also hope that this attempt to vindicate science for the concept and to present it in this, its own element, will know how to gain entry for itself through the inner truth of the matter.

We must be convinced that the true has the nature to prevail when its time has come, and that it appears only when this has come, and therefore never appears too early nor finds an unripe public; also that the individual needs this effect in order thereby to prove what is still its solitary affair and to experience as something universal the conviction that as yet belongs only to particularity.
But here the public is often to be distinguished from those who comport themselves as its representatives and spokesmen.
The former behaves in some respects differently from the latter, indeed even contrariwise.
If it good-naturedly rather takes upon itself the blame that a philosophical writing does not please it, these on the contrary, certain of their competence, shift all the blame onto the writer.
The effect is quieter in the former than the doings of these dead when they bury their dead.

If now general insight is on the whole more cultivated, its curiosity more alert and its judgement more quickly determined, so that the feet of those who will carry you out are already standing at the door, then the slower effect is often to be distinguished from this, an effect which corrects the attention that was forced by imposing assurances as well as the dismissive censure, and gives one part a contemporary world only after some time, while another has no posterity after this.
zh: 当我把科学借以存在的东西置于概念的自我运动之中，那么，那种认为我们时代关于真理的本性和形态的表象中已被列举出来的以及另外一些外在方面与此有出入、甚至完全相反的考察，看来并不会给那个要在上述规定中阐述科学体系的尝试许诺任何有利的接纳。

不过我可以想到，如果说例如柏拉图哲学的优异之物有时被放在它那些在科学上毫无价值的神话里，那么也曾经有过一些时代，它们甚至被称为狂热的时代，在其中，亚里士多德哲学因其思辨的深度而受到尊重，而柏拉图的《巴门尼德》，大概要算古代辩证法最伟大的艺术作品，被视为神圣生命的真的揭示和肯定的表达，并且尽管迷狂所产生的东西有许多浑浊，这种被误解的迷狂实际上本应不外乎纯粹概念，——而且我们时代哲学的优异之物把它的价值恰恰放在科学性之中，并且即使别人对此有不同的看法，实际上也只有通过科学性才让自己发挥作用。
因此我也可以希望，这个要把科学判归概念、并把它在这个它固有的要素中阐述出来的尝试，会懂得凭事情的内在真理为自己开辟入口。
我们必须确信，真的东西具有这样的本性：当它的时代到来时，它就会自行贯彻；而它只有在时代到来时才显现，因此从不会出现得太早，也不会找到一个不成熟的公众；同样，个体需要这种效果，以便借此检验那还只是它孤独的事情的东西，并把那种还只属于特殊性的确信经验为某种普遍的东西。
但在这里，常常要把公众与那些充当它的代表和代言人的人区分开来。
前者在某些方面与后者不同，甚至恰好相反。
如果它好心好意地宁愿把一部哲学著作不合自己口味这个罪过担在自己身上，那么这些人则确信自己有资格，把一切罪过都推到作者身上。
在前者那里，效果比这些死人埋葬他们的死人时的所作所为更安静。
如果现在普遍的识见总体上更有教养，它的好奇心更警觉，它的判断更快地确定下来，以至于那些将要把你抬出去的人的脚已经站在门前，那么往往要与此区分开那种更慢的效果，它既纠正那种通过声势逼人的保证被逼出来的注意力，也纠正那种不屑一顾的责难，并且要过些时候才给一部分人一个同时代的世界，而另一部分人在此之后却再也没有后世了。

en: Since, moreover, in a time in which the universality of spirit has grown so strong and individuality has, as is fitting, become so much the more indifferent, that universality also maintains itself in its full extent and cultivated wealth and demands it, the share that falls to the activity of the individual in the entire work of spirit can only be small; so the individual must, as the nature of science already entails, all the more forget itself, and indeed become and do what it can, but just as it may expect and demand less of itself and for itself, so too less must be demanded of it.
zh: 此外，在一个精神的普遍性如此强大、而个别性也如其所应当地变得如此无足轻重的时代里，这种普遍性还保持在它完整的规模和它那有教养的丰富之上，并且要求这种丰富，于是落在个体活动头上的、在精神的整个事业中的那一份就只能很小，所以个体就越发必须忘掉自己，正如科学的本性已经带来的那样，并且只管去成为和去做它所能成为和做到的，但人们同样也必须少要求它一些，正如它自己可以少期待于自己、少为自己要求一些。
